title: Make your first image
description: From opening Zephra to saving your first result. No technical background needed.

sections.title: Before you start
paragraphs: You need a Mac with Apple Silicon (an M-series chip) and macOS 15 or later. You can check your Mac in Apple menu → About This Mac.

The app and its models are separate downloads. A model is the creative engine that turns your description into an image or video. Start with one; you can add others later. Models need several gigabytes of storage, often much more during setup.

sections.title: Install and choose a model
steps: Open the downloaded DMG and drag Zephra into Applications. Open Zephra from Applications.
In the first-launch model chooser, read the recommendation for your Mac. Select a model and use the button that says Download, Build, or Continue, depending on what is already available.
Keep your internet connection available while files download. Zephra may then prepare the model locally. This first setup takes longer than opening a prepared model.
If you chose Skip for Now, use Choose a Model on the canvas to return to the chooser.

sections.title: Create something simple
steps: Choose an image model, such as FLUX.2 klein 4B or Z-Image Turbo, using the model menu at the top of the window.
Leave the small reference-image box empty. If a thumbnail is there, clear it with its × button.
Type the example below into the prompt box. A prompt is simply a description of what you want to see.
Keep the initial Size and Steps settings and choose 1 seed. Click Generate, or press Command–Return.
Wait until generation finishes. An in-progress preview can look blurry or unfinished; judge the completed image.
sections.prompt: A small copper robot reading a newspaper at a kitchen table. Morning light comes through a window on the left. A blue ceramic mug sits beside it. Warm, natural photography, eye-level view.

sections.title: Keep it or try again
paragraphs: Completed results are saved to your library automatically. The default folder is Pictures/Zephra. Right-click a result in Library and choose Export… to save a copy elsewhere.
To try another interpretation, right-click a generated result and choose Queue a Variation. Your previous result stays in the library.
